en: Points of Controversy Great Fifty-Section Fourth Chapter
The Discourse on the Abandoning of All Fetters:
Is the abandoning of all fetters Arahantship? Yes.
Is it not the case that all fetters are abandoned by the path of arahantship?
One should not say so... [etc. ...
Is it not the case that all fetters are abandoned by the path of arahantship?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does one abandon personality-belief, doubt, and adherence to rules and observances by means of the path of arahantship?
One should not speak thus … [and so on] … No.

Is it not the case that one abandons the view of a personal body (*sakkāyadiṭṭhi*), doubt (*vicikicchā*), and adherence to rules and observances (*sīlabbataparāmāsa*) by means of the path of arahantship?
Yes, it is.
But has the Blessed One not stated that the fruit of stream-entry (*sotāpattiphala*) is the abandoning of these three fetters (*saṃyojana*)?
“Yes.
“If the abandonment of the three fetters is stated by the Blessed One to be the fruit of stream-entry,
then indeed it should not be said that ‘all fetters are abandoned by the path of arahantship.’”
Is it the case that all fetters are abandoned by the path of arahantship?
Yes. Does one abandon gross sensual lust and gross ill-will by the path of arahantship? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does one abandon gross sensual desire and gross ill will by means of the path of arahantship?
Yes.
Is it not said by the Blessed One that the fruit of the once-returner is the attenuation of sensual lust and ill will?
Yes, it is.
If the fruit of the once-returner is indeed said by the Blessed One to be the attenuation of sensual lust and ill will, then surely it should not be said [that this is the fruit of the non-returner].
“By the path of arahantship, all fetters are abandoned.
Is it the case that by the path of arahantship all fetters are abandoned? Yes.
Does one abandon even the subtlest residual lust for sensual pleasure and even the subtlest residual ill-will by means of the path of Arahantship?
One should not say so... [as before] ...
Does one abandon even the subtlest residual lust for sensual pleasure and even the subtlest residual ill-will by means of the path of Arahantship?
“Yes.
“But has it not been stated by the Blessed One that the fruit of non-returning is the abandonment, without remainder, of sensual lust and ill will?
“Yes.”
If the Blessed One has stated that the fruit of non-returning is the complete abandonment of sensual lust and ill will, then surely it should not be said:
"All fetters are abandoned by the path of arahantship.
Is it the case that all fetters are abandoned by the path of arahantship?
“Yes.
“But has it not been stated by the Blessed One that Arahantship is the complete abandonment of attachment to form, attachment to the formless, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance?
“Yes.”
If, as stated by the Blessed One, Arahantship is the complete abandonment of sensual lust for the form realm, sensual lust for the formless realm, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance,
then surely it should not be said that "all fetters are abandoned by the path of Arahantship.
It should not be so stated.
“Is the abandonment of all fetters Arahantship?”—
Yes. But is it not the case that for an Arahant all fetters have been abandoned?
“Yes.
“If all fetters have been abandoned by an Arahant, then indeed it must be said:
‘The abandonment of all fetters is Arahantship.’”
The Discussion on the Abandoning of All Fetters is finished.
The Fourth Chapter.
Its summary verse:
The householder is an *arhat*; with birth, he is an *arhat*; all phenomena of an *arhat* are free from taints;
the *arhat* is endowed with the four fruits—in the same way, [he is endowed] with the six equanimities; through awakening, he is a Buddha; he is endowed with his own characteristics;
as a Bodhisatta, he has entered the certainty and lived the holy life; he is one who has practiced and is endowed with the fruit; [of all fetters...]
Abandonment is arahantship.
